title: Lock out a named breaker in a US panel with a clamp-on lockout and padlock
instruction: Lock out circuit 4, the breaker with the blue label: press the red clamp-on lockout onto its handle, turn the lockout's black knob until it grips the handle, close the lockout's lever, then put the padlock's shackle through the holes at the lever's end and snap it shut. Leave the other breakers as they are.
context: Before work on a circuit, its breaker is locked OFF with a lockout device and a personal padlock. A lockout on the wrong breaker, or one that is not clamped tight and padlocked, lets someone switch the circuit back on while a person is working on it.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top the bases stand on. Panel: a small grey steel load-centre tub (26 cm wide, 20 cm tall, 8 cm deep) is fixed to an upright plywood backboard (40 cm wide, 33 cm tall, 1.8 cm thick) that stands on the table and is fixed to it; the tub's steel deadfront faces the robot 31.0 cm in front of the bases, its centre line 3.0 cm left of the midline, spanning 10 cm right to 16 cm left of the midline and 10 to 30 cm above the table. Breakers: six Square D QO120 single-pole plug-on breakers (19 mm per space, 76 mm long, black) sit in two columns either side of a 4 cm centre strip, three rows 1.9 cm apart with the middle row 20.0 cm above the table; the left column (circuits 1, 3, 5 from the top) spans 5.0 to 12.6 cm left of the midline, the right column (circuits 2, 4, 6) 1.0 cm left to 6.6 cm right of it. Each handle (10 mm wide, about 11 mm proud of the deadfront) moves left-right: leaning toward the centre strip is ON (22 degrees), leaning outward is OFF (21 degrees). Circuit 4 (right column, middle row, handle 1.4 cm right of the midline) is OFF; the other five are ON. Labels: a colour-coded circuit label (18 x 17 mm, printed number) on the centre strip beside each breaker: 1 white, 3 green, 5 orange on the left; 2 yellow, 4 blue, 6 white on the right. Lockout: a Master Lock 493B Grip Tight circuit breaker lockout (red powder-coated steel channel 74 x 19.8 x 18.9 mm, 53 g: two side plates with serrated zinc jaws between them, a black knurled thumbscrew knob (15 mm across) left exposed past the plates' end, and the channel's end loop with an 8.3 mm padlock hole; a hinged red lever that, shut, covers the channel's open side and wraps the knob on top, bottom and end, with its own padlock tab over the loop), jaws open, lies in its installed orientation (open side toward the robot, slot toward the panel, knob end to the left) on two grey plastic posts (1.5 x 1.8 cm each, 19.1 cm tall, on a 6 x 5 x 1 cm foot) under its hinge end and its middle, with its rear edges 23.6 cm in front of the bases, spanning 9.0 to 16.4 cm right of the midline, centred 20.0 cm above the table; its lever is swung open 115 degrees about its hinge (the right end), sticking out toward the robot and to the right, its free half resting on a third post (1.6 x 1.6 cm, 19.1 cm tall). Padlock: a Master Lock 410 Zenex safety padlock (purple, 410PRP; thermoplastic body 38 mm wide, 45 mm tall, 19 mm thick; 6.35 mm steel shackle with 38 mm vertical and 20 mm horizontal clearance; 0.10 kg), unlocked with its shackle popped up 16 mm, stands upright on a grey plastic column (0.9 x 3.0 cm, 11.0 cm tall, on a 5 x 6 x 1 cm foot) 26.2 cm in front of the bases and 16.5 cm left of the midline, its legs side by side left-right with the free (short) leg on the right. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. Nothing else is on the table. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Score 0 if, before the after-release check, at any time: the lockout is clamped on, or sits pressed onto for 0.5 s or more, any breaker handle other than circuit 4's; any other breaker's handle moves 2 mm or more at its tip; or circuit 4's handle goes 6 degrees or more past the middle of its travel toward ON. Otherwise the score is the highest level reached: 0.25 if the lockout sits on circuit 4's handle (handle between the jaws, the lockout's rear edges within 3 mm of the deadfront, tilted under 10 degrees); 0.5 if the knob is also turned until the jaws grip the handle, before the lever is closed (the grips touch the handle: with the lever open, a 3 N pull straight off the panel moves the lockout less than 1 mm); 0.75 if the lever is also shut (within 6 degrees) over the tightened knob and the padlock's shackle passes through both holes at the knob end (the channel's loop and the lever's tab over it); 1.0 if the shackle is also latched shut through them and the after-release check passes. After-release check, done by the reviewer once both grippers have been at least 6 cm from the lockout and the padlock for 1 s: (1) hook a push-pull spring scale behind the lever's middle and pull it straight away from the panel at 20 N for 1 s; pass if the lever stays shut (opens less than 5 degrees, so the knob stays covered); only if it opened more than 20 degrees, (1b) turn the knob loosening with 0.1 N m for 1 s (a torque screwdriver bit on the knob); (2) pull the lockout straight off the panel at 20 N for 1.5 s; pass if it moves less than 3 mm; (3) push circuit 4's handle toward ON with 20 N, 15 mm from its pivot (0.3 N m; enough to switch a free handle ON), for 1 s, through the lockout; pass if the handle stays on the OFF side of the middle of its travel. All must pass for 1.0; a shut padlock that fails the check scores 0.75. Distances are read with a rule or from a photo with a scale in view.
reset_notes: Open the padlock with its key and take it out of the holes; swing the lockout's lever open, turn the knob back (anticlockwise seen from the knob end) about one turn until the jaws are 1 mm off the handle, and pull the lockout off; check circuit 4 is OFF and the other five ON; put the lockout back on its posts (open side toward the robot, knob end to the left, lever swung open 115 degrees onto its rest) and the open padlock back on its column, short leg to the right. About 2 minutes.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies on joints, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Geometry does the locking: the clamped body blocks the handle; the shut lever covers the knob; the shackle through both holes stops the lever opening. Rules: knob thread (inferred M8 pitch, self-locking), clamp force, lever cam, handle detent, padlock latch (no key). Sizes from 493B and QO120 data sheets; jaws, knob, lever read from photos. Simplified 6-space panel; checks in sim. Details in README.
